# Isolated legacy minimap foreground correctness proof

This is a source-bound correctness harness, not a game, performance benchmark, acceptance rerun, or release claim. It extracts the actual original759 `drawMap`, `drawMapLayer`, race paths and three delegate methods. It imports the actual original/candidate cinematic preset handlers and candidate foreground helper. The only replacement bindings are fixed fixture state/providers, a lexical sampled clock, real Canvas2D instances, and explicitly declared fault adapters. No producer body is recreated. No full game graph or public assets are built.

## Frozen scope

The original is75906273c0cd414c0d004320fc6f654b4783e5b1. The reviewed candidate source is1c06524e82012d1cecae2c7ac3d0bbf2abcbb355, treea0073ba042dcb59f128141eadb16006ca7a32c9e, with exactly six changed paths and sole parent759. `manifest.json` pins all source bytes/blobs and toolchain locks. `build.mjs` verifies source before and after extraction, checks the original schedule and absence of target backing-size writers, preserves the complete original foreground statements, and saves each exact UTF-16 span and SHA. Compilation uses the locked esbuild/TypeScript only for this fixture.

Reviewed source bindings are now selected for the first isolated proof publication. The manifest sets `executionBound:true`, selects the verified GitHub checkout binding, and pins the compiled fixture, refreshed extraction receipt, and proof source files. First browser execution is pending; no browser was launched during preparation. The workflow records its actual first attempt/head/run and exact manifest hash in a separate runtime binding, verifies the checked-out proof parent and exact file delta, and preserves that binding for an independent artifact audit. Missing or inconsistent bindings refuse browser launch. Native macOS Metal and Linux SwiftShader are separate paired lanes; cross-OS pixels are never compared.

## Exactly eight groups,26 raw pairs,four native screenshots

The full fixed order is `schedule.json`; all input numbers are `tapes.json`. The cases cover visible island/city drawings, three hidden updates and latest reveal, original hidden guards and CSS exposure, old background flushing and partial rebuild/blit failures, partial producer exceptions,8,192-command/unsupported fallback, native canonical state/current-path continuation, private source reset/native reset and separately labeled synthetic loss-listener policy.

All four composition pairs have **zero prior target readbacks**. They are P1 visible, P2 latest reveal, P4 failed background rebuild and P5 partial error. The native background raw checkpoint uses another pair. Each composition takes one native screenshot before the first `getImageData` call on either target; both actual canvases have420×290 CSS/backing dimensions, integer coordinates, DPR1 and the same opaque matte. There is no bitmap copy, scaling, color normalization, region mask or tolerance. The first screenshot also contains a third actual candidate-source canvas with one native opaque pixel changed, so the composition detector consumes no fifth screenshot. That canvas has no earlier readback either.

The raw detector flips exactly one saved candidate channel. A separate state-only detector changes a property without changing pixels; a path detector clears the native path before the common continuation. Positive path continuations use real native state/path behavior, not a fake Canvas model. Intentional detector mismatches are required and never substitute for positive equality.

The original immediate clear/blit remains native. Only foreground primitive paints can wait; packets own no image references. Inputs are sampled exactly once at fixed scheduled calls; reveal poisons all providers and invokes the actual preset handler. The helper runs no delayed producer. Unknown context methods and native invalid-argument faults are explicit fixture cases, not claims that the helper implements arbitrary Canvas semantics. Source absence of post-init target width/height writes is part of the contract. Synthetic `contextlost`/`contextrestored` is listener-policy evidence only; no real browser loss or generic unowned-reset equivalence is claimed.

## Bounds and failure behavior

Two lanes, eight sequential groups,26 paired raw checkpoints (maximum32), four screenshots. The driver uses Node performance.now for its180s absolute budget, including source preflight and teardown; wall timestamps are separate receipts. Work stops by170s to reserve at most10s cleanup; each group has20s, launch at most30s, outer job10min. Every browser/protocol setup await is bounded under the same work deadline, and an expired budget refuses invocation instead of passing Playwright timeout0. Graceful close leaves the final second of the same cleanup budget for an owned force-stop; an expired or unconfirmed stop remains failed. One owned browser server per lane; unexpected disconnect, late output, timeout, failed close or unconfirmed process exit keeps the capture partial. There is no retry. The workflow retains failed capture and audit outcomes independently.

Raw bytes total25,334,400B per lane. All screenshots/metadata are limited to8MiB including a4MiB PNG subcap; total output40MiB. Regular writes reserve1MiB for capture-status.json,64KiB for a terminal failure receipt, and1MiB for audit.json inside those unchanged caps. Partial writes are charged before I/O. Neither driver nor auditor writes an out-of-cap fallback; if even a bounded report cannot fit, the audit emits failure to stdout and creates no extra file. The decoder accepts only bounded8-bit non-interlaced RGB/RGBA PNGs, verifies chunk CRC/zlib EOF, and compares exact same-image regions. Saved source/bundle/workflow pins, state, provider calls, native method/property coverage, errors and cleanup receipts are independently checked. The composition auditor requires the exact ordered canvas rectangles at(10,10),(450,10), and only for P1 the detector at(890,10), all420×290. Each composition must reference its own checkpoint PNG with the exact ledger byte count/SHA; comparing a rectangle with itself or reusing another screenshot fails. Only the fixed local fixture HTML/JS URLs and an explicitly benign204 favicon are allowed. Unexpected requests, response errors, failed requests, console/page errors and ledger overflow invalidate the capture. Error and network receipts have fixed count/byte caps inside the reserved status slot. Completed evidence is preserved after any failure; an incomplete capture cannot pass merely because some images match.

Readback can affect browser storage decisions. The fresh-pair rule avoids normalizing the four composition cases with prior raw reads. The separate WebGL renderer attestation identifies the requested browser lane; it does not prove which storage backend Canvas2D chose. Passing this proof establishes only these fixed pixels/state/lifecycle cases. It demonstrates no lower GPU allocation, game-frame time, controls completion time, or release readiness.

## Source-only preparation commands

`node build.mjs ORIGINAL_ROOT CANDIDATE_ROOT LOCKED_GAME_TOOLCHAIN OUTPUT_DIR` compiles the small bundle and records exact source spans. `node --test offline.test.mjs` and `python offline_test.py` exercise only scope/binding/comparator/PNG/readback-schedule contracts. They do not launch browsers. The reviewed workflow is prepared for its first controlled execution; no browser run occurred during source-only preparation.

## Browser identity correction before first execution

The exact products are pinned per lane: Metal Chrome/158.0.8127.89 and SwiftShader Chrome/158.0.8127.88, as independently retained in prior proof artifacts. Metal retains its previously verified CDP revision1de57fa19722fa6d6841d4f596c394d015580656. No retained Linux CDP revision was available. The software lane therefore requires and records a valid actual40-hex revision during this first capture, explicitly marked previouslyVerified:false; it does not borrow Metal’s revision or assert cross-platform commit equality. Both original and candidate execute in the same browser instance within each lane. Wrong products, missing/malformed revisions, or an incorrect known Metal revision fail. This policy is selected before execution, not relaxed after observing a result. Manifest evidence fields pin the retained product/revision receipts.

## Retained workflow validation failure and context correction

The first published orchestration, PR279 head54ad35659973dc5f60f7b638afb5f57e08ba544e, produced run46044456787 attempt1 with failure and zero jobs/check-runs. No browser ran. The connector did not expose the validation annotation, so no exact GitHub error text is asserted here. Source review independently identified three `runner.temp` expressions under job-level `env`, where the [official context availability table](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability) does not allow `runner`.

This corrected workflow removes those three job-level expressions and writes the same MINIMAP_COMPILED, MINIMAP_OUTPUT and MINIMAP_BINDING paths from RUNNER_TEMP into GITHUB_ENV in the first setup step after the attempt guard. The artifact upload's step-level `runner.temp` remains valid and unchanged. The original failed orchestration is retained; this copy is intended for a separate proof branch with the same sole production parent. Cases, source/runtime pins, bundle, drivers, pixel comparisons and limits are unchanged. First browser execution remains pending.
